title: IFERROR: readable fallbacks for #DIV/0!
summary: Wrap sell-through and stock cover divisions in IFERROR so new stores and zero sales show a clear message.

blocks.text: A new store has not received stock yet, so its sell-through is sold divided by zero received. Excel shows #DIV/0!. In a report that goes to head office, that looks like a mistake.
Your job is to build sell-through and stock cover formulas that stay readable when a division is impossible. IFERROR replaces an error with a message you choose.

items: Objective: use IFERROR to replace errors with a useful fallback.
You pass the mission at 75% or more in the Assessment.

blocks.text: IFERROR returns the first argument. If that is an error, it returns the second argument instead.
Sold divided by received. If received is 0, show No stock instead of #DIV/0!.
Dividing by zero is impossible, so Excel returns #DIV/0!. Other errors exist too, such as #VALUE! when you do arithmetic on text. IFERROR catches all of them.
Tip: choose a fallback that tells the reader what happened. A message such as No stock is better than 0, because 0 looks like a real result: a store that received stock and sold none.
Tip: IFERROR also hides your own mistakes, such as a wrong cell reference that causes an error. Check the formula without IFERROR first, then wrap it.
Four questions on IFERROR. Type numbers without commas, for example 0.4.

items: IFERROR(value, value_if_error) replaces any error with your fallback.
Pick a fallback that explains the situation, not one that looks like data.
Check the plain formula first, because IFERROR also hides genuine mistakes.

items.prompt: C2 holds 180 units sold and B2 holds 240 units received. What does =IFERROR(C2/B2,0) return? Give the decimal.
A new store has received no stock. Which fallback is best in a sell-through column?

options.label: "No stock", because it explains why there is no percentage
0, because it keeps the column numeric
